title: Right derived functor on bounded below derived categories, computed on bounded below complexes of injectives
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], $\mathcal A$ with enough injectives (every object is a subobject of an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]), and $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ an additive functor. For an abelian category $\mathcal C$ let $K^+(\mathcal C)$ be the full subcategory of the homotopy category of cochain complexes of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] whose objects are the bounded below complexes ($L^n=0$ for $n\ll0$), let $D^+(\mathcal C)$ be the bounded below derived category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] and $Q^+_{\mathcal C}:K^+(\mathcal C)\to D^+(\mathcal C)$ the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms; let $K^+(v):K^+(\mathcal A)\to K^+(\mathcal B)$ be $v$ applied termwise (it respects homotopies since $v$ is additive). Then: (1) there are a functor $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ and a natural transformation $\alpha:Q^+_{\mathcal B}\circ K^+(v)\to Rv\circ Q^+_{\mathcal A}$ such that $(Rv,\alpha)$ is a right derived functor of $v$, i.e. a left Kan extension of $Q^+_{\mathcal B}\circ K^+(v)$ along $Q^+_{\mathcal A}$: for every functor $G:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ and every natural transformation $\beta:Q^+_{\mathcal B}\circ K^+(v)\to G\circ Q^+_{\mathcal A}$ there is a unique natural transformation $\gamma:Rv\to G$ with $\gamma_{Q^+_{\mathcal A}L}\circ\alpha_L=\beta_L$ for all $L$; (2) for every bounded below complex $I$ of injective objects of $\mathcal A$ the morphism $\alpha_I:Q^+_{\mathcal B}(v(I))\to Rv(Q^+_{\mathcal A}I)$ is an isomorphism; (3) if $(Rv',\alpha')$ is another pair with the property of (1), there is a unique isomorphism $\theta:Rv\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv'$ with $\theta_{Q^+_{\mathcal A}L}\circ\alpha_L=\alpha'_L$ for all $L$.

source.place: Lemma 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), part (2): for A with enough injectives and an additive F: A -> B, RF: D^+(A) -> D^+(B) is everywhere defined; Lemma 05TH (lemma-injective-acyclic), part (1), cited in its proof: a bounded below complex of injectives computes RF (clause (2)); Section 05S7 (section-derived-functors), Definition 05S9 (RF defined at X, its value) and Lemma 05SA (lemma-derived-functor: the values are functorial, uniquely). Mathlib defines RF as a left Kan extension along the localization (clauses (1), (3)), which is the derived functor of Stacks where it is everywhere defined.
